(a) Establishment.—The Administrator of the Federal Aviation Administration shall establish a special task force to be known as the FAA Task Force on Air Carrier Safety and Pilot Training (in this section referred to as the “Task Force”). 
    (b) Composition.—The Task Force shall consist of members appointed by the Administrator and shall include air carrier representatives, labor union representatives, and aviation safety experts with knowledge of foreign and domestic regulatory requirements for flight crewmember education and training. 
    (c) Duties.—The duties of the Task Force shall include, at a minimum, evaluating best practices in the air carrier industry and providing recommendations in the following areas:
        (1) Air carrier management responsibilities for flight crewmember education and support. 
        (2) Flight crewmember professional standards. 
        (3) Flight crewmember training standards and performance. 
        (4) Mentoring and information sharing between air carriers.  
    (d) Report.—Not later than one year after the date of enactment of this Act, and before the last day of each one-year period thereafter until termination of the Task Force, the Task Force shall submit to the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure of the House of Representatives and the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation of the Senate a report detailing—
        (1) the progress of the Task Force in identifying best practices in the air carrier industry; 
        (2) the progress of air carriers and labor unions in implementing the best practices identified by the Task Force; 
        (3) recommendations of the Task Force, if any, for legislative or regulatory actions; 
        (4) the progress of air carriers and labor unions in implementing training-related, nonregulatory actions recommended by the Administrator; and 
        (5) the progress of air carriers in developing specific programs to share safety data and ensure implementation of the most effective safety practices.  
    (e) Termination.—The Task Force shall terminate on September 30, 2012. 
    (f) Applicability of Federal Advisory Committee Act.—The Federal Advisory Committee Act (5 U.S.C. App.) shall not apply to the Task Force.

fable.w: The section creates an FAA task force whose members include air carriers, labor unions and outside safety experts, and it is charged with evaluating best practices and making recommendations, including for legislative or regulatory action. That is an advisory body with non-federal members, which brings outsiders into federal decisionmaking. The tempting reading is that this is only a report to congressional committees, exempt from the Federal Advisory Committee Act, and so stays inside the government. That reading fails because the participation lies in the outside membership and advisory role, not in the reporting channel.
fable.s: The Task Force shall consist of members appointed by the Administrator and shall include air carrier representatives, labor union representatives, and aviation safety experts

opus.w: The FAA Administrator must set up a task force that includes outside parties: air carrier representatives, labor union representatives, and aviation safety experts. It gives recommendations on pilot training and professional standards, including possible regulatory actions. That makes it an advisory panel with non-federal members, which counts as participation. Neither the report to congressional committees nor the FACA exemption changes the fact that outsiders are brought into federal decisions on aviation safety.
opus.s: The Task Force shall consist of members appointed by the Administrator and shall include air carrier representatives, labor union representatives, and aviation safety experts with knowledge of foreign and domestic regulatory requirements for flight crewmember education and training.
opus.b: **Tempting-but-wrong reading:** The task force reports to congressional committees, and FACA expressly does not apply to it, so this could look like a purely internal arrangement that stays inside the government. That reading fails because of who sits on the task force: air carrier representatives, labor union representatives, and outside safety experts. These are non-federal parties. They recommend best practices and possible regulatory actions on federal pilot training standards to the FAA. Whether FACA applies doesn't decide whether outsiders take part.

qwen_chat.w: The section establishes a Task Force that explicitly includes non-federal members such as air carrier representatives, labor union representatives, and aviation safety experts. According to the definition, an advisory committee or panel that includes non-federal members constitutes participation. Although the Federal Advisory Committee Act does not apply, the substantive requirement to include outside stakeholders in the advisory process meets the criteria for participation.
qwen_chat.s: (b) Composition.—The Task Force shall consist of members appointed by the Administrator and shall include air carrier representatives, labor union representatives, and aviation safety experts with knowledge of foreign and domestic regulatory requirements for flight crewmember education and training.
qwen_chat.b:
Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue "No" because the Task Force reports to Congress (inside government) and the Federal Advisory Committee Act is explicitly excluded, suggesting it is an internal agency working group. However, the definition of participation focuses on whether non-federal parties are involved in the decision-making or advisory process. The text explicitly mandates the inclusion of outside parties.

Why it fails: The definition states that participation includes an advisory committee, board, or panel that includes non-federal members. Subsection (b) explicitly requires the Task Force to include "air carrier representatives, labor union representatives, and aviation safety experts." These are entities and individuals outside the federal government. Their inclusion in a body that provides recommendations to the Administrator and Congress constitutes participation as defined.
